one_line: An early Buddhist rock‑cut specialist crafting chaitya halls in the western Deccan around 200 BCE–170 CE.

appearance.age_look: mid-30s, lean and wiry from physical labour, average height but compact and strong
appearance.face: oval face with sharp cheekbones, medium-brown Deccan complexion, sun‑darkened skin, straight nose, faint stubble shadow on jaw, a slim vertical scar on the right eyebrow; calm, focused default expression with slightly furrowed brows as if judging rock strata
appearance.hair: thick black hair pulled back into a short, tidy knot low at the back of the head, with a few loose strands near the temples; simple narrow cloth headband in dull red wrapped across the forehead to catch sweat
appearance.costume: era-accurate artisan outfit: a knee-length, off-white cotton angarkha-style wrap tunic crossing left over right and tied with thin inner ties, the fabric slightly worn and marked with fine stone dust; beneath it, a plain light-brown cotton dhoti wrapped firmly and ending mid-calf, with neat pleats at the front; around the waist, a dark indigo cotton cloth belt/sash knotted at the left hip, from which hang a small simple bronze plumb bob and a wooden measuring rod; on the shoulders, a pale ochre cotton uttariya (shawl) draped from the left shoulder across the chest and around the back, ready to be pulled over the head against dust; feet in simple dark brown leather sandals with toe loops; minimal jewellery—one thin bronze bangle on the right wrist and small plain bronze ear studs—signalling modest artisan status rather than elite wealth
appearance.signature: a long wooden measuring staff held in the left hand, marked with carved notches, with a simple bronze plumb bob tied by a cord at one end to check vertical lines while he stands, the staff often braced against his shoulder like a surveyor’s tool

ref_desc: A mid-30s lean Deccan cave engineer with medium-brown skin, black hair in a short back knot and red headband, wearing an off-white wrap tunic, light-brown dhoti, indigo sash, ochre shawl and sandals, always carrying a notched wooden measuring staff with a bronze plumb bob.
sheet_prompt: Draw a full-body anime-style character sheet of a mid-30s early Buddhist Deccan cave engineer: a lean, wiry man with medium-brown sun-darkened skin, an oval face with sharp cheekbones and a slim scar through his right eyebrow, calm focused eyes and a faint stubble shadow; his thick black hair is tied into a short knot low at the back of his head, with a few loose strands at the temples and a narrow dull red cloth headband across his forehead to catch sweat. He wears era-accurate, modest artisan clothing: a knee-length off-white cotton wrap tunic crossing left over right, slightly worn and dust-marked, over a firmly wrapped light-brown cotton dhoti ending mid-calf with neat pleats; a dark indigo cotton sash is tied around his waist, with a small bronze plumb bob and a short wooden measuring rod hanging from it, and a pale ochre cotton shawl (uttariya) is draped from his left shoulder across his chest and around his back, ready to pull over his head, while his feet are in simple dark brown leather sandals with toe loops. Add minimal jewellery: a thin bronze bangle on his right wrist and small plain bronze ear studs. His signature prop is a long wooden measuring staff marked with carved notches and a bronze plumb bob on a cord at one end, which he holds in his left hand or rests against his shoulder like a surveyor’s tool. Use a restrained palette of off-white, light brown, indigo blue, dull red and pale ochre, and present him from front, side and back to clearly show his face, hair knot and headband, tunic, dhoti, sash, shawl, sandals and measuring staff.
